analysis:
Constellation Energy fell 2.4%, outperforming both the broader market's 4.4% decline and its AI power and infrastructure peers, which dropped a median of 7.7%. The 5.3 percentage point gap versus peers and the company-specific attribution suggest this move was driven more by CEG holding up relatively well than by sector-wide developments. Headlines point to data center policy concerns and questions about valuation, though one item discusses the broader AI trade weakening and two focus on peer Vistra's challenges around a Texas election vote rather than CEG directly.

The stock reports Q3 earnings in four days. CEG's recent earnings history shows a typical move of around 1.8 percentage points beyond what the market explains, with three of the last five estimate beats followed by negative abnormal moves—including the two most recent reports, which beat by 11.7% and 5.3% yet both saw the stock lag the market the next session.
